turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not suffer you to underestimate the threat of the Mussulmans, Sandip. They are a restless and discontented people, and it is only a matter of time before they rise up against the likes of you and me.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Nikhil, have you considered the possibility that these threats are being used as a means to an end, rather than a genuine concern for our safety?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not indulge in speculation, Bimala. My concern is the immediate threat to our people and property.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I see that you both are deeply concerned about the situation. What steps have you taken to prepare for any potential threat?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What's the world coming to? First, it's the Englishmen, now it's the Mussulmans. Can't I even enjoy a peaceful afternoon without some self-proclaimed hero trying to scare me?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, the situation is grave. I've received credible reports of a Mussulman gang planning to raid our villages, and I will not stand idly by while you dismiss the threat.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so full of dramatic flair. I'm shaking in my boots at the prospect of a few ragtag Mussulmans raiding our villages. What's the world coming to, that I need your warning to protect my own land?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your sarcasm, Sandip. The threat is real and I will not stand idly by while your dismissiveness puts our people at risk. I have reports of a growing resentment among the Mussulmans towards our lands.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, the great seer of doom and gloom, always predicting the worst. What's next, will you tell me the crops will wither and the rains will fail as well?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your flippant attitude, Sandip, will be your undoing one of these days. I'm warning you, not as a rival, but as a responsible zamindar, of the very real threats that our lands face.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, please, Nikhil, spare me the dramatics. I'm not running a risk of being attacked by the Mussulmans, I'm being courted by their charming son, Rashid.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, do not underestimate the situation. Rashid's overtures are a ruse, and his father, the Maulvi, is fueling the flames of discord in our region.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so serious and full of dire warnings. What's the world coming to when even the Maulvi's son can't get a decent cup of cha without stirring up trouble?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your frivolity, Sandip. The threats from the Mussulmans are genuine and must be taken seriously.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, come now, Nikhil, don't be such a worrywart. I'm sure the Mussulmans are just itching to attack my precious estate because of my legendary hospitality.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I implore you, Sandip, to take this threat seriously. Your estate is not invincible, and I will not stand idly by if you refuse to take precautions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always warning me of impending doom. Can't you see I'm busy enjoying my own private little utopia here?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your levity is misplaced, Sandip. The situation is dire and requires serious consideration.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, don't be such a bore. Can't you see I'm busy enjoying the sunshine?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, the situation with the Mussulmans is grave and I will not be ignored.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
